summary: Android renders every button label in a heavier, nearly black weight; React uses regular-weight text with state-specific brown, magenta, white, and gray colors.
Palette diverges significantly: Android uses saturated yellow and pink, a paler green for Continue, and a darker disabled fill, while React uses lighter pastels and a darker green.
Android adds pronounced lower-right drop shadows and slightly rounder corners; the React buttons are flat with thin borders.
Button bounds differ slightly: Android top-row buttons are shorter around the same centerline, while widths and second-row positions drift right by a few pixels.
A thin pale vertical strip appears near the Android panel's right edge with no React counterpart.
likelyCauses: Android is inheriting default native button typography, elevation, and corner-radius styles instead of shared design tokens.
React state color tokens were not mapped to the Android button variants.
Android is using intrinsic text measurement or padding rather than explicit React-matched dimensions.
The extra right-edge strip may be an unintended divider, indicator, or container decoration.
analysis.suggestedOwner: Android design-system or button-component owner
suggestedFixes: Apply regular font weight, React-matched font sizes, and the correct per-state label colors instead of forcing black text.
Map Sync, Delete, Continue, and disabled backgrounds to the exact React color tokens.
Remove button elevation or shadow and match the React corner radius and thin border treatment.
Set explicit heights, widths, paddings, gaps, and label alignment from the React component specification.
Remove or hide the pale vertical element near the Android right edge.

likelyCauses: Android conditionally omits the actions block or fails to enable it for an owner role.
Description and role fields are populated from different data or fallback states across platforms.
Android divider tokens use a different color and thickness from the shared design.
Avatar sizing, icon stroke, and empty-state font-style tokens are not mapped consistently.
The Android toolbar uses the wrong icon resource.
analysis.suggestedOwner: Android UI engineer
suggestedFixes: Render the ACTIONS heading and red full-width "Remove Member" button with React-equivalent bounds, or hide them on both platforms.
Align the description and role values, and restore React's help icon beside the Role label.
Use the same divider color and stroke thickness throughout all profile sections.
Match React's main avatar size, icon proportions, and italic empty-state typography.
Replace the Android speech-bubble icon with the React person/plus icon.
